title: vault-quickunlock — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_quick_unlock_blob_raw + protocol::decode_quick_unlock_blob — the MYQ1 vault.quickunlock device-local credential codec (MYND-329; §9.14). The blob wraps a THIRD copy of root_key (32 bytes) under a provider-supplied wrap_key. The codec is PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC: it never runs Argon2id, so wrap_key is supplied DIRECTLY as a fixed input (the PIN→wrap_key Argon2id derivation is pinned separately in the argon2id family, input_path 'quickunlock-pin'). provider_kind (0x01 biometric / 0x02 PIN) and account_number_hash both bind via aad_quick_unlock_blob (AAD role 'quick-unlock-blob'); there is NO HKDF SubkeyRole (a root_key-derived KEK would be circular since the blob protects root_key). ciphertext_len is the fixed constant 64 (root_key 32 + CTX tag 32), so there is no size cap / ciphertext_len_overflow case — an off-value is CiphertextLenInvalid. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip to the unwrapped root_key), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per §6.4, incl. the provider_kind-flip which is AAD-bound), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per QuickUnlockBlobError decode variant). Reference impl: protocol/src/quick_unlock_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec: docs/spec/protocol.md §9.14 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-quickunlock/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_wrap_key_hex.description: 32-byte symmetric wrap_key (hex), supplied DIRECTLY. The codec is provider-agnostic — it never derives this key. For the PIN provider it is the Argon2id output (the derivation is pinned in the argon2id family); for the biometric provider it is the Keychain secret.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound (together with provider_kind) into the 47-byte AAD via aad_quick_unlock_blob (role string 'quick-unlock-blob').

input_provider_kind.description: Wrap-key provider: 0x01 = macOS-biometric (Keychain), 0x02 = PIN (Argon2id). Written into the public header at offset 5 AND bound into the AAD so a biometric-minted blob cannot be reinterpreted as a PIN blob.

input_pin_salt_hex.description: 16-byte pin_salt (hex) written into the public header at offset 6. The Argon2id salt for the PIN provider; all-zero when provider_kind != PIN. NOT bound into the AAD (it is public so a PIN caller can read it back before decode).

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex) — the secret being wrapped (the third device-local copy). This is the AEAD plaintext, NOT a key-derivation input.

input_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

expected_vault_quickunlock_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output, hex-encoded lowercase. Always exactly 114 bytes (228 hex chars): 50-byte header + 32-byte root_key ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_root_key_hex.description: The recovered 32-byte root_key (hex) — the unwrapped third copy.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: QuickUnlockBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault (wrong account_number_hash) vs tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong wrap_key vs provider_kind-flip (provider_kind is AAD-bound) beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects (bad magic, unregistered provider_kind, wrong ciphertext_len, etc.) are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / provider_kind / ciphertext_len checks all run before the AEAD stage (spec §9.14.1 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: QuickUnlockBlobError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, ProviderKindUnsupported, CiphertextLenInvalid, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated}). NOTE there is no 'ciphertext_len_overflow' here (unlike vault-search/indices): the quick-unlock ciphertext_len is the fixed constant 64, so any off-value is the exact 'ciphertext_len_invalid' reject. A provider_kind that is a REGISTERED value (0x01/0x02) but mismatches the AAD-bound value is a decrypt_aead_fail, not a parse_fail.
